note: Growth and keep for the creatures the family holds (roadmap item 56, first part). Years are the world clock's (pass_time). A creature is an egg (egg-layers only), then young, adult, elder, and dies of old age; how long each lasts is set by its size class. Keeping costs gold each year, paid from the heir's gold; unpaid years sink its mood, and at no mood an egg spoils and a creature wanders off. No dice are drawn: the length of an elder's life varies with a value taken from the dynasty seed and the creature's id. The Ranch is the family house's third track (GameHouse): each level adds pens, a hatchery for eggs and a nursery for the young (the `ranch` table). Creatures can be sold or set free. Grown creatures can work (`work_of`): wool, eggs and venom earn gold each year, and guards turn away a share of the gold an event would take. A creature works only while its mood holds. Farm animals (sheep, cattle, pigs, chickens: `farm` in creatures.json) are bought young at a town's market, give wool, milk or eggs through the year (by season, and less when kept poorly) and can be slaughtered for meat and hide: see data/creatures/farm.json and GameFarm.

levels.about: A shed and a field: no more places than the family's own six.
Pens for 3 more, and a hatchery: eggs cost half as much to keep and spoil slowly.
Pens for 6 more, and a nursery: the young cost less to keep and take neglect better.
Pens for 9 more, a warm hatchery and a big nursery: the cheapest keep and the gentlest.
